title: A Sharp Threshold Bound for Monotone Graph Properties
main_claim: Friedgut–Kalai conjecture: for every nontrivial monotone graph property on n vertices and every 0<ε<1/2, p_{1-ε}-p_ε ≤ 2^19 log(1/(2ε))/(log n)^2. It is derived from Var_p(f) ≤ 2^17 I_p(f)/(log n)^2 for every vertex-symmetric Boolean f and every p.
coverage: I read all of the LaTeX: introduction, fourier, graph, threshold and the figure. Every step was checked by hand. (1) Lemma 2.1, the scalar 4th-moment inequality with ρ=σ/4: the coefficients 13σ²/32 and 9σ²/256 are correct, and so is the bound ≤(a²+b²)². The tensorization by induction with the L² triangle inequality is valid. The bound ||u||_4 ≤ ρ^{-d}||u||_2 on low-degree functions and the duality step giving ||P_{≤d}v||_2 ≤ ρ^{-d}||v||_{4/3} are correct. So are the derivative identity hat h(A∪i)=σ hat{Δ_i h}(A), ||Δ_i h||_{4/3}^2=I_i^{3/2}, ρ^{-2k}=m^{σlog(4/σ)/32} ≤ m^{1/16}, and the case split on I ≤ m^{1/4}, which gives σ²m^{-5/16} I. (2) Lemma 3.1, the restriction identity: correct by orthonormality in y. (3) Prop 3.2: f_y is invariant under Sym(B). The orbits on F_B have size C(m,2) or m, both ≥ m since m ≥ 3, so I_e(f_y) ≤ I(f_y)/m. The lemma's bound is linear in I, so averaging over y is fine, and Pr(e∈F_B) ≤ 2m/n. (4) Lemma 3.3: a nonisolated vertex of minimum degree has degree ≤ 2s/v ≤ √(2s) ≤ k, since s ≤ C(v,2). We have v ≤ 2s ≤ k². On the event B∩V(S)={u}, S∩F_B is exactly the set of edges at u. The union bound and the estimate t²e^{-t/2} < 1/2 for t ≥ 16 hold, giving the capture probability ≥ m/(2n) and the constant 4m^{-1/4}. (5) Thm 1.2: the tail bound is 2σ²/k² = 8192/(log m)², so σ cancels exactly. The bounds log m ≥ t/3, 73728+165 < 2^17, and the small-n case (Var ≤ σ²I ≤ I/4 ≤ 64 I/(log n)²) all check out. (6) Thm 1.1: Russo's formula μ'=I_p for monotone f, then log-odds integration, give width ≤ 2C_0 log((1-ε)/ε)/(log n)². Also log((1-ε)/ε) ≤ 2log(1/(2ε)) holds because 4ε(1-ε) ≤ 1, giving 2^19. I also sanity-checked the bound on examples: clique, edge-count majority, max degree, and small p where Poincaré makes it trivial. None contradicts it.
sibling_notes: The family 186 board was empty when I read it. The paper cites two companion papers (ExpectationEquivalence2026, SecondKahnKalai2026) but does not use them in the proof, so there is no circular dependence.
